f.pc.appearance.o: Human, about eighteen; wears simple traveler's clothes

f.t3.m6.d3_2.1.o: a notice board papered with slips stands just within the door

f.t5.m10.d1.1.o: Alaric's name, entered in the Guild ledger

f.t5.m10.d2_2.1.o: F, read from the counter crystal and noted in the ledger

f.t6.m12.d2.1.o: a Guild notice on broker fees for monster materials, the year's price list, and a town-council-sealed warning about the ford on the river road

f.t6.m12.d5_2.1.o: new postings come with the morning cart, midday most days; private work is talked about in the hall

f.t7.m14.d1.1.o: A moss-grown hill half a day east of Ashbridge off the old quarry track; goblins dug tunnels into it, palisades of sharpened sticks at the mouths, scouts on the surface, warriors in the first tunnel l

f.t7.m14.d2_2.1.o: First floor is F work, deeper is E

f.t7.m14.d3_3.1.o: Dried goblin ears are the standard proof of a kill and fetch two coppers each through the Guild broker, the standing rate

f.t7.m14.d4_4.1.o: A shaman's ear is worth roughly five silver by the clerk's uncertain memory; the exact price list hangs on the Guild board

f.t7.m14.d5_5.1.o: The Guild logs adventurers in and out of the Warrens under a crown charter, at no cost, so a search party knows when someone went in

f.t7.m14.d6_6.1.o: The shaman has thrown fire down the second tunnel more than once

f.t7.m14.d7_7.1.o: Two lads together took a goblin contract for the Warrens this morning; she warns Alaric, F-ranked and new, not to go alone

f.t7.m14.d8_8.1.o: The real money in goblins is their stolen stash — farm tools, kettles, odd silver; the Guild takes no cut of found goods, only brokered materials

f.t8.m16.d2_2.1.o: If he is not out by the next dawn after entry, the charter has the clerk tell the town watch, who send whoever is cheap and willing; nobody rides out fast for a Novice

f.t8.m16.d4_3.1.o: She advises drinking water before setting out and warns not to drink the water near the goblin hill, though the hill itself is damp

f.t9.m18.d6_2.1.o: stone-circle well at the center, stalls in a loose ring, baker on the north side, fish stall, smith by its hammering, general store two doors along

f.t10.m20.d2.1.o: the fish stall outside the market sells smoked herring, three for a copper

f.t13.m26.d1.1.o: sharpened stakes driven deep, the work of hands that knew stakes; no sentry visible at the tunnel mouth

f.t14.m28.d2.1.o: fire-hardened stakes thick as a wrist, driven close enough that only a hand could pass between them

f.t14.m28.d3_2.1.o: a passage eight feet high and wide, raw-cut earth shored with split timber, bending left about fifteen paces in; goblin leavings and a fire-blackened cooking circle just inside; fresh small bare footp

f.t15.m30.d2.1.o: Inside the tunnel mouth: fire-blackened circle with goblin leavings, timber shoring, trodden mud churned with goblin prints

f.t17.m34.d4_3.1.o: wooden club studded with chips of stone (lying within reach, not held)

f.t19.m38.d2.1.o: Many unshod feet and chattering voices swelled through the tunnels behind Alaric as he fled, then rose to a brief chorus and cut off; whether they found the brute's body is unknown

f.t19.m38.d4_3.1.o: Stiff hide cinched with a knot, clacking faintly; its contents unknown until opened

f.t20.m40.d2.1.o: jammed tight; contents shift with a clack of hard things, something roundish and something faintly metallic; needs a knife-edge, fire or time to cut the cord

f.t22.m44.d2_2.1.o: the midday cart arrived an hour ago, but no new contracts are posted yet; the postmaster's man is copying the rolls and they will be posted in the morning

f.t22.m44.d4_4.1.o: the Guild brokers materials like ears, tusks and hides for a cut, but found goods it does not touch; Alaric must sell those himself in town

f.t22.m44.d5_5.1.o: eleven copper with foreign faces, a brooch, a resin lump, meat, and the dented locket

f.t22.m44.d8_6.1.o: a locket that rings is somebody's locket, dented and stolen off a neck more like; the smith will open it and read whatever name is inside — think on whether you want to know it

f.t23.m46.d3_3.1.o: nothing tonight that pays; sleep or drink

f.t23.m46.d4_4.1.o: nothing paying tonight; the watch sometimes wants a body for gate work — ask at the barracks on the morrow; talk the tannery is short of hands for the lime pits; new postings on the board come morning

f.t24.m48.d6_4.1.o: a snap-hinge underneath the dent, good work, somebody's paid-for thing; the dent and old handling green suggest it was lost hard, and she warns its contents will be Alaric's name to answer for

f.t25.m50.d3.1.o: a brittle curl of hair tied with thread and a folded paper note reading 'Trud. Back by harvest. — E.'

f.t25.m50.d4_2.1.o: the locket came here off a goblin's neck, and the name Trud is not rare — half the valley has one

f.t26.m52.d1.1.o: no — she knows no one in the valley named Trud and doesn't know who went missing where

f.t26.m52.d2_2.1.o: the Warrens take people every month; some come out, some don't, and mostly nobody makes a noise about it

f.t26.m52.d3_3.1.o: the Watch would not pay for news of a missing name without a body or survivor — they'd want something worth more than paper

f.t26.m52.d4_4.1.o: the Guild logs every soul that goes into the Warrens, in and out, under crown charter; a ledger line would show when a Trud went in and never came out — worth checking, costs nothing but the walk

f.t27.m54.d4_2.1.o: the great board behind the desk stands bare of anything new until morning

f.t28.m56.d2.1.o: Trud Askel's-son is a farm lad off the quarry track who went into the Warrens for goblin teeth

f.t28.m56.d3_2.1.o: goblin teeth pay a copper apiece at the broker

f.t29.m58.d1.1.o: saw the opened locket with the note 'Trud. Back by harvest. — E.' and a curl of pale hair, and read the note twice

f.t29.m58.d3_2.1.o: the Warrens entry ledger says Trud Askel's-son entered alone

f.t29.m58.d4_3.1.o: Trud's name and a note 'Back by harvest — E.' came off a goblin in the Warrens

f.t30.m60.d1.1.o: Quarry track is the east road past the south gate; ask at the gatehouse where the farms start

f.t31.m62.d3.1.o: pottage and bread plus a loft bed for two coppers

f.t33.m66.d3.1.o: passed at dawn: a cluster of thatch around a stone barn, hens in the yard

f.t33.m66.d4_2.1.o: passed: a long low house with thin smithy smoke rising behind it

f.t34.m68.d5_3.1.o: Trud Askel's-son is his sister's lad; Trud went down the Mossback Warrens near three weeks ago and the family has heard nothing since

f.t35.m70.d2.1.o: Trud, whose name and lock of hair were in the locket, was the smith's kin (son); he had been missing nineteen days, last word promising to return by harvest

f.t35.m70.d3_2.1.o: Trud was killed by goblins in the Mossback Warrens; Alaric found the locket on a goblin there and found no sign of Trud alive

f.t35.m70.d6_5.1.o: asks Alaric to give him an hour to tell Trud's mother in his own way, then wants to hear everything Alaric found in the Warrens — where, how many goblins, what he saw of Trud

f.t36.m72.d4.1.o: came out with red-rimmed eyes after the better part of two hours; his wife's sister is dead and a priest has been sent for

f.t37.m74.d3_2.1.o: His kin Trud went missing in the Mossback Warrens nineteen days ago; there is a burial to see to and a sister the smith cannot leave this week.

f.t37.m74.d4_3.1.o: Locals call it Mossback; lads dare each other past the first chamber, the smith's father cut stone from its mouth, and there have been no goblins in it in the smith's lifetime.

f.t37.m74.d5_4.1.o: He reasons more goblins than the four burned must hold the camp, and the drag marks a day old may or may not be Trud.

f.t37.m74.d7_5.1.o: He says the Guild will post the warrens as F-rank work and that a bounty is due from the Guild for goblin work besides what he can pay.

f.t38.m76.d1.1.o: two silver from his own purse for going back into the Mossback Warrens, plus whatever Guild bounty comes for goblin heads, and a third silver if Alaric brings Trud's remains home

f.t39.m78.d2.1.o: edged and finished; the smith handed it over handle-first, paid for

f.t39.m78.d3_2.1.o: will draw the ground on slate tonight — the fork, the quarry cut, his father's pillar stones — and have something hot ready at first light

f.t40.m80.d2.1.o: the corner of the barn to sleep the afternoon, clean hay, and will wake Alaric at first light

f.t40.m80.d6_4.1.o: to be in and out of the smithy through the day, hammering quietly; the bellows already going

f.t41.m82.d1.1.o: nosed Alaric awake-friendly in the barn, then went back to its hay

f.t42.m84.d4.1.o: lends Alaric the chalked slate — his to carry, not to keep; bring it back as proof he came out

f.t42.m84.d5_2.1.o: has a burial to see to this week and a sister; will not watch Alaric walk out to the hill

f.t43.m86.d6.1.o: near full from the smith's jug

f.t43.m86.d7_2.1.o: lantern, flint and slate to Alaric, all to be returned

f.t43.m86.d8_3.1.o: a hot meal if Alaric comes back with slate, lantern and flint

f.t43.m86.d10_5.1.o: yard gate is the left one; the moss-grown hill is the far side of the quarry track, half an hour's walk

f.t44.m88.d3.1.o: an old shallow trough cut through the moss near the quarry mouth, grass returning along its edges, running down toward the quarry cut and into the dark of it

f.t44.m88.d4_2.1.o: a cold rain-sodden ash ring with stones just inside the hill's mouth, a torn sandal and a cracked cup by the fire stones, nothing worth carrying

f.t44.m88.d5_3.1.o: past the entrance the fork lies ahead in the dark: the quarry cut going left, the low passage going right

f.t45.m90.d2.1.o: many fresh small bare long-toed prints in the wet floor, going both ways, coming out of a side crack in the right-hand wall and running deeper down the passage

f.t47.m94.d3.1.o: Dressed granite pillar stones prop the hill every dozen strides, older than the quarrymen's work

f.t47.m94.d4_2.1.o: Dozens of small bare long-toed footprints, all running down, and one wider drag groove with boot-heel edges beside it, descending with them

f.t47.m94.d7_5.1.o: Faint yellowish flickering light not Alaric's, and a smell of old smoke with something sour and living beneath it, beyond the right-hand dogleg

f.t48.m96.d4_2.1.o: the three-taps-pause-two knocking is made by the goblin striking the wall with a rod of pale wood

f.t48.m96.d8_5.1.o: a tall quarry-cutting chamber with a low coal fire in a ring of stacked bones and broken pillar-chunks, five goblins around it, and behind the sleepers a dragged bundle with a booted foot at the dark

f.t50.m100.d3.1.o: the goblins did not follow Alaric up the low passage

f.t50.m100.d4_2.1.o: the goblins kicked out and scattered their fire ring, putting out their light in the chamber below

f.t51.m102.d3.1.o: low cloud, rain not far off

f.t51.m102.d4_2.1.o: nothing followed him up; nothing came out of the mouth

f.t52.m104.d8_3.1.o: the drover's woman came by yesterday, third time this week

f.t52.m104.d10_4.1.o: a brindled dog chained by the gate, and the drover's knife still on the rack by the grinding wheel, waiting for its edge

f.t53.m106.d1.1.o: Trud Askel's-son, the smith's sister's son, nineteen days overdue taking bar-iron to the river market

f.t54.m108.d4_3.1.o: will send Marta only after Alaric tells her the plan; she does not follow a stranger into the dark on a nod

f.t54.m108.d5_4.1.o: goblins drag meat home to whatever keeps it, or whoever — he reads the drag marks the same way Alaric does

f.t55.m110.d2_2.1.o: has a wife who works the forge with him; she lives in the house across the yard

f.t55.m110.d4_3.1.o: tells Alaric not to tell Marta that Trud is alive and well: she goes for the truth and to bring back what can be brought

f.t56.m112.d2_2.1.o: round shield strapped to her forearm and a short-hafted axe

f.t56.m112.d8_3.1.o: the shortsword was bought off a quarry man who went east; Brant offers it, saying it wants a hand that will blood it

f.t57.m114.d3.1.o: the lantern, taken herself for the march

f.t57.m114.d4_2.1.o: says Alaric checks his gear like a drover, not like a mage

f.t61.m140.d4_3.1.o: the goblins beyond the barricade have gone from sight behind stone and into side cracks, holding still and waiting

f.t62.m142.d3_2.1.o: stayed at the barricade behind, shield up, holding it

f.t62.m142.d4_3.1.o: swept flat stone with a burnt-smelling clay bowl, animal bones stuck in cracks and heaped in corners — pig skulls, deer legs, a sheep's ribcage lashed with cord

f.t62.m142.d5_4.1.o: the drag furrows run on through the low right-hand crawl; the left opening smells of rot and wet thatch

f.t62.m142.d9_5.1.o: long knee-height scratches and a small four-fingered handprint in old mud along the passage — something small braced itself while dragging

f.t63.m144.d1.1.o: a stub of pale willow wood, one hole, mouth end burned smooth, four rough recent notches cut along its side

f.t63.m144.d2_2.1.o: the whistle's rope runs taut across the chamber at ankle height and crosses the mouth of the low crawl, both ends fixed into stone cracks — an alarm line that would sound the whistle if anyone crawls

f.t63.m144.d3_3.1.o: under a missed corner of silt on the flat stone beside the burnt bowl: a scratch of the same four-notched mark as on the whistle, beside a second mark, a circle with a bar — somebody kept count here

memories.text: first saw {pc} at Adventurers' Guild hall, Ashbridge
Adventurers' Guild hall, Ashbridge: {pc}: "I walk along the road into Ashbridge and look for the Adventurers' Guild."
Adventurers' Guild hall, Ashbridge: {pc}: "I approach the counter. "Good morning. I'd like to register with the Guild and see what contracts are available for a new mage.""
Adventurers' Guild hall, Ashbridge: {pc}: "I count out two silver and slide them across the counter. "Yes, please register me.""
Adventurers' Guild hall, Ashbridge: {pc}: "I take the plate and go to the notice board to read the posted contracts."
Adventurers' Guild hall, Ashbridge: {pc}: "I ask the clerk, "Tell me about the Mossback Warrens — what's in there, and what do goblin parts fetch through the Guild broker?""
Adventurers' Guild hall, Ashbridge: {pc}: ""Please log me into the Mossback Warrens ledger." Then I ask her where in town I can buy rations, a waterskin and other cheap supplies before I set out."
first saw {pc} at General store opposite the smith
General store opposite the smith: {pc}: "I head to the market square and go into the general store opposite the smith."
General store opposite the smith: {pc}: "I'll take the waterskin and a length of rope. What does the hardtack cost, and do you have dried rations for a few days?"
General store opposite the smith: {pc}: "I'll take four pieces of hardtack, two bundles of the dried rations, and a flask of lamp oil."
On the way to Mossback Warrens: {pc}: "I sling my pack and head out on the quarry track east toward the Mossback Warrens."

memories.text: On the way to Mossback Warrens: {pc}: "I skirt the flooded quarry along the shelf and approach the near tunnel mouth from downwind, watching for movement before closing in."
memories.place: On the way to Mossback Warrens

memories.text: On the way to Mossback Warrens: {pc}: "I wait a few more moments behind the gorse, then move up the bare slope low and quiet, stopping short of the stakes to peer into the tunnel mouth."
memories.place: On the way to Mossback Warrens

memories.text: On the way to Mossback Warrens: {pc}: "I slip between the stakes and ease into the tunnel mouth, staff ready, hugging the wall toward the bend."
memories.place: On the way to Mossback Warrens

memories.text: On the way to Mossback Warrens: {pc}: "I hold still at the bend and listen, waiting to see if the thing beyond the turn moves again before I risk a look."
memories.place: On the way to Mossback Warrens

memories.text: On the way to Mossback Warrens: {pc}: "I put my eye carefully around the corner post for a quick look at what lies beyond the bend."
memories.place: On the way to Mossback Warrens

memories.place: On the way to Mossback Warrens

memories.text: Open slope before the moss-grown hill: {pc}: "I grab the sling-bag and knife from the dead brute, then slip back around the bend and retreat quietly out of the tunnel."
memories.place: Open slope before the moss-grown hill

memories.text: Ashbridge: {pc}: "I head down the quarry track toward town, opening the sling-bag as I walk to see what's inside."
Ashbridge: {pc}: "I cut the sling-bag's cord with the brute knife and look through what's inside."

Adventurers' Guild hall, Ashbridge: {pc}: "I take the sling-bag and locket inside the Guild hall and ask whether the midday contract cart has arrived and whether anyone here can buy goblin loot or open a"
first saw {pc} at Adventurers' Guild hall, Ashbridge
first saw {pc} at Adventurers' Guild hall, Ashbridge
Adventurers' Guild hall, Ashbridge: {pc}: "I walk over to the far tables and ask the hunters and dice players if any of them know of paid work tonight."
first saw {pc} at Marta's smithy
first saw {pc} at Marta's smithy
Marta's smithy: {pc}: "I head to the smithy and ask Marta whether she can open the dented locket, and what she'd charge."
Marta's smithy: {pc}: ""I'm sure. Go ahead—ease it open.""
Marta's smithy: {pc}: "I ask Marta if she knows anyone in the valley named Trud who went missing near the Warrens, and whether the Watch would pay for news of it."
Adventurers' Guild hall, Ashbridge: {pc}: "I thank Marta and head back to the Guild hall to check their ledger for a Trud who entered the Warrens and never came out."
The clerk checked the ledger for {pc}: Trud Askel's-son entered the Warrens alone nineteen days ago and never signed out; she warned him again not to go alone
Adventurers' Guild hall, Ashbridge: {pc}: "I ask her to check the ledger for a Trud who entered the Warrens and never signed out."

The clerk and the grey-stubbled hunter saw the locket taken off a goblin in the Warrens, with Trud's name and the note 'Back by harvest. — E.' inside; the hunter said it will be bones and boots by now, nineteen days on.

Adventurers' Guild hall, Ashbridge: {pc}: "I show her the opened locket. "This came off a goblin in the Warrens today—Trud's name inside, and a curl of hair. Does the Guild post a contract for something "
first saw {pc} at The Wether's Head
The Wether's Head: {pc}: ""Understood. I'll take the locket to his kin on the quarry track tomorrow. Good night." I pocket the locket and head out to find cheap lodging for the night."
The Wether's Head loft: {pc}: "I take the pottage and bread and a loft bed, and pay her the two copper."
The Wether's Head: {pc}: "I sleep through the night and head down at dawn for the morning meal."
the fork under the thorn tree: {pc}: "I take the bread and dripping and pay her the copper, then eat and set out for the south gate."
memories.place: the fork under the thorn tree

memories.text: A stranger with a staff came to the door at morning carrying news of Trud from the Warrens
first saw {pc} at the Brant place
the Brant place: {pc}: "I walk to the Brant place and knock, asking for Trud Askel's-son's kin: "I'm carrying news of Trud from the Warrens. Are his folk here?""
The smith took the opened locket with Trud's name and lock of hair, read the note, and stood wet-eyed and furious learning goblins in the Warrens had taken his kin
the Brant place: {pc}: "I hold out the opened locket. "This came off a goblin in the Warrens yesterday. Trud's name inside, and a lock of hair. I'm sorry—I found no sign of him alive.""
the Brant place: {pc}: "I wait the hour, keeping out of the way in the yard until the smith comes back out."
The smith heard the whole account of the warrens without fidgeting, eyed the staff when the fire was told, and set his cup down untasted at the drag marks; a woman's voice rose once from the house.
the Brant place: {pc}: "I drink, then give him the whole account: the two dead men at the first chamber, the goblin camp with the brute and its knife, the fire I put into them, where t"
the Brant place: {pc}: ""I'll go back in. What coin are you offering, and have you work here at the forge—a blade or a mail shirt I could buy or borrow before I go?""
The smith edged the drover's knife for {pc}, talked of the drover who never came back, and promised a slate map of the ground and a hot meal before first light
the Brant place: {pc}: ""Yes to the knife—edge it and I'll pay your eight copper. And I'll go at first light, not today—I want full daylight and fresh legs for the low passage.""
first saw {pc} at the Brant place
the Brant place: {pc}: "I take the knife and buckle it on my belt where I can reach it fast, then ask if there's a corner of the yard or barn where I can sleep the afternoon before fir"
the Brant place: {pc}: "I thank him, push the horse's nose off if it comes nosing, and settle into the barn corner with the blanket to sleep until first light."
the Brant place: {pc}: "I eat the porridge while it's hot, then go over the slate with him and tell him I mean to start down the low passage, right at the fork, as far as my light lets"
the Brant place: {pc}: "I tell him the truth: I've a flask of lamp oil and that's all—no lantern of my own and no flint. I ask if he'll lend me the horn lantern and a flint, and how mu"
Open slope before the moss-grown hill: {pc}: "I take the lantern, flint and filled flask, thank him, and set off through the yard gate for the hill."
memories.place: Open slope before the moss-grown hill

memories.text: Open slope before the moss-grown hill: {pc}: "I light the lantern with the strike-a-light, check the flame is steady, and walk in past the cold ashes toward the fork, taking the low passage on the right."
memories.place: Open slope before the moss-grown hill

memories.text: Open slope before the moss-grown hill: {pc}: "I stop past the crack, keep the lantern raised, and watch the side crack for movement while readying Arcane Bolt in my free hand."
memories.place: Open slope before the moss-grown hill

memories.text: Open slope before the moss-grown hill: {pc}: "I edge past the crack and creep down the low passage after the prints, lantern low, listening between steps."
memories.place: Open slope before the moss-grown hill

memories.text: Open slope before the moss-grown hill: {pc}: "I peer around the bend toward the firelight, staying hidden behind the split pillar, and count whatever is making that light."
memories.place: Open slope before the moss-grown hill

memories.text: Open slope before the moss-grown hill: {pc}: "I back away from the bend as quietly as I came, keeping low behind the pillar, and slip back up the low passage toward the fork."
memories.place: Open slope before the moss-grown hill

memories.text: the fork under the thorn tree: {pc}: "I back away from the bend and retreat up the low passage toward the fork, ready to run if they follow."
memories.place: the fork under the thorn tree

memories.text: Open slope before the moss-grown hill: {pc}: "I head back up the wider passage toward the entry cutting and daylight, keeping the lantern low and listening as I go."
memories.place: Open slope before the moss-grown hill

memories.text: The smith saw {pc} return alive from the Mossback Warrens and hand back the slate, lantern and strike-a-light

thread.t6.1.text: The hunters confirm the new postings go up on the board in the morning

thread.t13.1.text: The arguing voices became many padding feet and chattering that chased him the length of the first passage, then cut off — the warrens are roused behind him

thread.t15.1.text: Beyond the bend: the unseen thing gnawed at food, grunted, crossed the passage and settled onto stone; its slow sleeping rasp reaches Alaric if he strains.
thread.t15.1.resolution: Alaric's look past the corner post showed the creature itself

thread.t21.1.text: The innkeeper confirms the quarry track route: south gate, east road, first farms where the ground lifts — Kettleby, then the Brant place, then the fork; everyone out there knows everyone's trouble.

thread.t35.1.text: The smith is ready to hear the full account: 'you're the only man left who can tell it'
thread.t35.1.resolution: Alaric told him everything over the cup; the smith took it in and turned to what comes next.

thread.t43.1.text: The smith's promised meal is served at the bench; the knife's edge still owed
thread.t43.1.resolution: the smith ground the drover's knife to a true edge and set it on the bench within Alaric's reach

thread.t44.1.text: The drag groove continues down the pillar passage, one clean furrow through the mud with boot-heel edges pressed beside it
thread.t44.1.resolution: the groove's other end is in the firelit chamber: a bundle and a boot on a foot still in it, dragging toward the dark at the back

thread.t45.1.text: The knocking came again far ahead and below: three flat taps, a pause, then two, then stopped as if someone caught themselves
thread.t45.1.resolution: the sound is a goblin tapping the chamber wall with a pale wood rod, idle and purposeless

thread.t49.1.text: The deeper voice from the dark at the chamber's back rose in a slow climbing note that silenced the goblins' yammering

thread.t49.2.text: A booted foot twitches in the bundle behind the sleepers — someone bound or hidden among the goblins

thread.t50.1.text: The three-taps-two rhythm sounded again, faint and far, from somewhere new in the warrens — not the chamber

thread.t53.1.text: The smith asks what Alaric made of the drag marks and the dark at the back of the chamber before saying anything else

thread.t55.1.text: Marta still waits at the open gate for Alaric's direct answer whether he'd take her in and what he'd want of her

thread.t59.1.text: The metal-hammering from behind the barricade stopped as Alaric charged.
thread.t59.1.resolution: the hammering ceased and did not resume after Alaric crossed the barricade

thread.t62.1.text: A wooden whistle hangs turning on a rope loop between the two ways out of the bone chamber

thread.t63.1.text: Someone strung the alarm line across the low crawl and kept a tally of comings and goings by the crawl; the whistle is loose in its loop, made to be lifted and blown, and was hung back after each pass

actions: 1. GOES — to Low crawl beyond the chamber (the story decides whether and where he arrives). Carry the way forward in this reply until he arrives, something acts on him, or a real choice of way appears; a sound, a shadow or a track without consequence is passed in a clause, never a stop.
extra: DUNGEON AHEAD (the engine's) — going on into a part of level 1 he has not seen: there he meets 3 goblin warriors. That is where this walk ends; bring exactly these, and the quiet way there is told in passing (a sound, a shadow or old tracks without consequence are no stop).
If he goes DOWN to level 2 instead, the first part there holds The Moss Shaman (goblin shaman).

resolutions.quote: I step over the trip-line without touching it, then crawl through the low passage slowly, watching for more lines ahead.

last.input: I step over the trip-line without touching it, then crawl through the low passage slowly, watching for more lines ahead.

inputs.input: I sit at the bench, eat the meal, and tell him what's down there: five goblins, the chamber with the drag marks, and a boot heel at the back of it — and I ask who the missing drover is.

"The drag marks run deep, not out — and whatever was at the back of that dark was still warm enough for the goblins to keep. If Trud's alive, he's deeper in, past the five I saw. I can't take five alone, but with better gear and a plan, I'd

"Marta takes the shield and lantern at the front and holds the goblins' charge; I flank from the bend's dark and hit them with Flame Lance. If something bigger keeps Trud deeper, we don't fight it — we cut him free and run. And I'll want th

"I'd have you at the front with shield and lantern, holding their charge while I flank and burn them. We go for truth, not hope — find Trud or what's left, cut free, and run before whatever keeps him wakes. I'll not promise you he's alive."
"When." I take up the leaf-bladed shortsword and belt it on, then check my gear before we march. #equipment
"Dusk tomorrow — understood. If we're not out, don't send anyone." I nod to Marta and head through the gate with her, up the quarry track toward the warrens.
"Ready. I'll watch our back." I follow Marta in, quiet, staff in hand.
I attack the goblin at the barricade with my staff.
I climb over the goblin barricade to get past it.
I follow the drag marks down the passage, moving carefully.
I examine the wooden whistle on the rope before touching it.
I step over the trip-line without touching it, then crawl through the low passage slowly, watching for more lines ahead.

deltas.name: stone lip opening over the chamber

desc: three goblins at a ringed hearth, two breaking old bones into a clay pot, one standing apart talking low to itself; their axes and a short spear lean against the wall, not on them

deltas.evidence: None of them had looked toward the crawl; the two went on chopping, the standing one talked with its back half-turned.

deltas.o: The drag marks run the whole crawl, smeared a body's width, and end at a low stone shelf in the fire-lit chamber beyond, where a roughly man-sized shape lies covered with a hide.

deltas.text: The drag marks end at a covered man-sized shape on a stone shelf in the goblins' fire-lit chamber — likely what is left of Trud.
